hardenings_applied_after_review: Guard: cheap-direction geo conflict (IP=CH + resolved EUR country, no verified company) → reviewRequired=true (GEO_WEAK_CONFLICT), instead of a silent EUR checkout. Same-currency and reverse (more-expensive) geo conflicts stay allowed+logged (rule 6). Tests added.
Checkout route: PRODUCTION_DISABLED decoupled from NODE_ENV — requireProduction = isProd OR live-Stripe-keys, so a misconfigured non-production host with live keys still fails closed.
E2E proof: fixed the loading-race capture of the unknown-state selector; now asserted in the verdict (initialSelectPrompt + initialNoPrice).
disclosed_residual_limitations: IP is never proof (stated by the spec): a fully-anonymous Swiss buyer who both spoofs an FR IP AND self-selects FR is not caught pre-payment; enforcement then relies on Stripe-collected card/billing/tax country at/after payment (webhook already captures currency). A hard pre-payment guarantee for unverified buyers would require Stripe billing-country restriction / post-payment reconciliation — recommended before high-risk launch, listed as a production-gate consideration.
Dev-mode price/amount mismatch check is non-blocking (console.warn) by design; anti-abuse unaffected (price is canon-derived). Hard-blocks in production.
Audit default sink is the structured server log; durable persistence is an unapplied DRAFT (owner approval required).
